info.title: roadbeat Studio API — Pro — Governance & Access
info.description:
Self-hosted headless CMS — Content Management & Publishing API

**Pro — Governance & Access.** Advanced roles and the role editor, SSO integration, tamper-evident audit logging with retention and compliance reports, and white-labeling.

get.summary: List all permission rules

200.description: Every rule of the organization, ordered by descending priority, then role, then content type.

post.summary: Create a new permission rule

201.description: The newly inserted rule as stored (server-assigned id and timestamps).

400.description: Validation failed — the request body does not match the documented schema (unknown properties are rejected).

get.summary: List rules for a specific role

200.description: Rules scoped to this role slug (both content-type-specific and fallback rules); empty array when none exist.

get.summary: List rules for a specific user

200.description: Rules scoped to this individual user (`user_id` set); role-level rules that also affect the user are NOT included.

get.summary: List rules for a specific content type

200.description: Rules that apply to this content type, including the organization-wide fallback rules (`content_type_id` = null).

get.summary: Get a permission rule by ID

200.description: The rule; 404 when it does not exist in the caller organization.
The rule after the update (unchanged when the body contained no writable field).

400.description: Validation failed — the request body does not match the documented schema (unknown properties are rejected).

post.summary: Set permissions for a content type + role (upsert)

201.description: The created or updated rule for that content type + role pair (`user_id` is always null).

400.description: Validation failed — the request body does not match the documented schema (unknown properties are rejected).

post.summary: Check if a user can perform an action on a content type (self; other users admin-only)

201.description: The verdict plus the full evaluation trace. Identical to what enforcement decides, so preview and reality cannot disagree.

400.description: Validation failed — the request body does not match the documented schema (unknown properties are rejected).

post.summary: Resolve effective permissions for a user + content type (self; other users admin-only)

201.description: Effective allowed action set for that user + content type, the deciding rule, and the ordered evaluation trace. Note this is the raw layered result and does NOT apply the admin bypass — use POST /check for the enforced verdict.

get.summary: Get permission matrix for the current user across all content types

200.description: One row per content type in the organization, ordered by name, with a boolean per action.

get.summary: Get permission matrix for a specific user (admin only)

200.description: One row per content type for the target user. Returns an empty array (not 404) when the user does not exist in the caller organization.

get.summary: Get content types the current user can create

200.description: Content types for which the caller's effective permissions include 'create', ordered by name.

get.summary: Get permission rule statistics

200.description: Aggregate rule counts for the caller organization.

get.summary: List all roles (CE defaults + custom)

200.description: CE's three built-in roles first (admin, editor, viewer — enriched from their system mirror row when one exists), then the organization's custom roles by slug. Each entry carries the number of users currently assigned.

post.summary: Create a custom role

201.description: The newly created custom role (`isCustom` true, `userCount` 0). 409 when the slug is one of CE's reserved role names or already taken in the organization.

400.description: Validation failed — the request body does not match the documented schema (unknown properties are rejected).

get.summary: Get role details with all permissions

200.description: Role metadata plus its resource grid and per-content-type rules. For CE built-in roles the resource grid is the hardcoded CE default and the content-type list is empty.

The role after the update. When at least one field actually changed, `userCount` comes back as 0 rather than the real assignment count — call GET /pro/roles for that. 400 when the slug refers to a CE built-in role.

400.description: Validation failed — the request body does not match the documented schema (unknown properties are rejected).

delete.summary: Delete a custom role (must have no users)

post.summary: Duplicate a role with all its permissions

201.description: The new role. Its resource and content-type permissions are copied from the source role but are not part of this response — read them via GET /pro/roles/{slug}.

400.description: Validation failed — the request body does not match the documented schema (unknown properties are rejected).

get.summary: Compare two roles side by side

200.description: Both roles, the resource-level and content-type-level differences (identical entries omitted), and aggregate counts.

get.summary: Get resource-level permissions for a role

200.description: Only the rows actually stored for this role slug, ordered by resource. Resources without a stored grant are absent (use GET /pro/roles/{slug}/matrix for a complete grid). Always empty for CE built-in roles.

post.summary: Set a single resource permission for a role

201.description: The upserted grant as stored.

post.summary: Set multiple resource permissions for a role at once

201.description: The upserted grants in request order. Applied one by one, not transactionally — a validation error part-way through leaves the earlier grants written.

delete.summary: Remove a resource permission for a role

get.summary: Get full permission matrix for a role (resources + content types)

200.description: Complete grid: one entry for every known resource (empty `actions` where nothing is granted) plus the content-type-specific rules. `isReadOnly` is true for CE built-in roles served from hardcoded defaults.

post.summary: Seed system role mirrors for CE roles (admin, editor, viewer)

201.description: Only the mirrors created by this call; idempotent, so an empty array means all three already existed.

get.summary: Get role editor statistics

200.description: Aggregate role and permission counts for the caller organization.

get.summary: Query the organization's audit log with filters and paging

200.description: Matching audit entries, newest first (raw `pro_audit_logs` rows, snake_case). Alongside `data` the body carries a sibling `total` (integer) — the full match count ignoring `limit`/`offset`. It is NOT the standard `meta` pagination block: the controller returns `{ data, total }` and CE's TransformInterceptor passes that through unchanged.

post.summary: Manually append an audit entry (admin only)

201.description: The stored entry, including the freshly computed `prev_hash`/`entry_hash` chain links. The actor, IP, user-agent and `source: "manual"` are stamped server-side from the authenticated request and cannot be supplied by the caller. A `changes` object sent in the body goes through the same redaction as platform-computed diffs (IMP-PRO-AUDIT-06): secret-like field names become `[REDACTED]` and oversized values are truncated before the row is persisted and hashed, so the echoed entry can differ from what was posted.

400.description: Validation failed — the request body does not match the documented schema (unknown properties are rejected).

get.summary: Get a single audit log entry by ID

200.description: The audit entry. `data` is null (still HTTP 200) when no entry with that ID exists inside the caller's organization.

get.summary: Get the audit history of one specific resource

200.description: Audit entries for that resource, newest first, capped by `limit` (default 50).

get.summary: Get the audit history of actions performed by one user

200.description: Audit entries whose actor is that user, newest first, capped by `limit` (default 50). Empty after a GDPR erasure scrub, which rewrites the subject's `user_id` to a pseudonym.

get.summary: Export audit logs as a JSON or CSV file

200.description: Success. JSON responses are wrapped in the standard envelope: `{ "data": ... }`, with optional `meta` (e.g. pagination) on list endpoints.

meta.description: Optional metadata (pagination, counts) — present on list endpoints

get.summary: List the organization's audit retention policies

200.description: All retention policies (enabled and disabled), newest first.

post.summary: Create an audit retention policy (admin only)

201.description: The created policy as stored, including DB-applied defaults.

400.description: Validation failed — the request body does not match the documented schema (unknown properties are rejected).

put.summary: Update an audit retention policy (admin only)

200.description: The policy after the update. `data` is null (still HTTP 200) when no policy with that ID exists in the caller's organization.

400.description: Validation failed — the request body does not match the documented schema (unknown properties are rejected).

delete.summary: Delete an audit retention policy (admin only)

200.description: `success` is false when no matching policy existed in the caller's organization.

post.summary: Run audit retention enforcement immediately (admin only)

200.description: Deletion counts overall and per enabled policy. Any policy that pruned rows also appends a `retention_checkpoint` audit entry recording the pruned tail hash, so the surviving hash chain stays verifiable.

get.summary: Verify the organization's tamper-evident audit hash chain (admin only) — detects careless or accidental modification and truncation, not a privileged direct-database writer

200.description: Chain verification outcome. Returns only aggregate chain state and the first broken entry ID — no hashes and no keys, and the chain digests are unkeyed SHA-256 in any case. That unkeyed construction bounds what the result can mean: `valid: true` says the trail is internally consistent (nothing was edited, re-ordered, dropped or re-attributed without the chain being rebuilt) and that any pruned history is anchored by a retention checkpoint. It is NOT proof of integrity against an attacker with write access to `pro_audit_logs`, who can rewrite entries and recompute a chain that verifies clean — protection against that comes from the append-only trigger, least-privilege database credentials and off-host log shipping. The verification run itself is appended to the chain as an `audit_verify` entry.

get.summary: Get audit log statistics for the dashboard

200.description: Aggregate counts scoped to the caller's organization. Count maps omit values that do not occur in the data rather than reporting them as zero.

get.summary: List saved audit searches (own plus shared)

200.description: The caller's own saved searches plus every search shared inside the organization, newest first.

post.summary: Create a saved audit search

201.description: The created saved search as stored; `user_id` is always the authenticated caller.

400.description: Validation failed — the request body does not match the documented schema (unknown properties are rejected).

200.description: The saved search after the update. Only the owner's own rows are written, but the row is then re-read org-scoped — so updating a shared search owned by someone else returns it unchanged, and `data` is null (HTTP 200) when the ID does not exist in the organization.

400.description: Validation failed — the request body does not match the documented schema (unknown properties are rejected).

200.description: `success` is false when nothing matched — unknown ID, another organization, or a search owned by a different user.

get.summary: List the available compliance report types

200.description: All report types with an `available` flag stating whether the underlying event source is wired on this host. Generating an unavailable type is rejected with 400.

post.summary: Generate a compliance report as JSON

200.description: The report with a per-type summary and the matching audit entries (capped at 10 000 rows; `totalEntries` is the uncapped count). Entries include the `prev_hash`/`entry_hash` chain columns so the report can be verified independently.

400.description: Validation failed — the request body does not match the documented schema (unknown properties are rejected).

post.summary: Export a compliance report as a JSON or CSV file

201.description: Success. JSON responses are wrapped in the standard envelope: `{ "data": ... }`, with optional `meta` (e.g. pagination) on list endpoints.

meta.description: Optional metadata (pagination, counts) — present on list endpoints

400.description: Validation failed — the request body does not match the documented schema (unknown properties are rejected).

get.summary: Get the organization's SSO configuration (secrets masked)

200.description: The raw `pro_sso_configs` row (snake_case column names) with every secret rewritten: the client secret becomes a fixed bullet string, the certificate is cut to its first 50 characters and the SCIM token is reduced to `<hint>••••••••`; `scim_token_hash` and `scim_token_hint` are removed entirely. `data` is `null` when the organization has no SSO configuration.

post.summary: Create the SSO configuration for the organization

201.description: The inserted `pro_sso_configs` row as returned by `RETURNING *`, with the same secret masking `GET /pro/sso/config` applies: `client_secret` becomes a fixed bullet string and `scim_token_hash` / `scim_token_hint` are removed entirely. The certificate is NOT truncated here. When SCIM was enabled, `scim_token` carries the plaintext bearer token — masking deliberately preserves it, and this response is the only place it ever appears.

400.description: Validation failed — the request body does not match the documented schema (unknown properties are rejected).

200.description: The re-read `pro_sso_configs` row, masked exactly as `GET /pro/sso/config` masks it: `client_secret` becomes a fixed bullet string and `scim_token_hash` / `scim_token_hint` are removed entirely. The certificate is NOT truncated here. When this update enables SCIM and the configuration has no token yet, a token is minted and `scim_token` carries it in plaintext — shown once, like on create; only its hash is stored. Otherwise `scim_token` is the `<hint>••••••••` preview when a hashed token exists, else `null` — re-enabling SCIM keeps an existing token valid; POST /pro/sso/config/regenerate-scim-token replaces it.

400.description: Validation failed — the request body does not match the documented schema (unknown properties are rejected).

200.description: Acknowledgement. The delete cascades to role mappings and stored IdP certificates; it is idempotent — deleting a non-existent configuration also answers `{ success: true }`.

post.summary: Import / refresh IdP metadata from the configured metadata URL

200.description: What the metadata document yielded: the parsed entity ID and SSO URL (both written to the configuration when present) and the number of signing certificates that now form the active verification set. No certificate material is returned.

get.summary: List the stored IdP certificates with their expiry

200.description: Active and retired IdP certificates, newest first, mapped to camelCase and enriched with the remaining days until expiry. The PEM itself is deliberately not included. An empty array is returned when the certificate service is unavailable or no SSO configuration exists.

post.summary: Generate a new SCIM bearer token (invalidates the previous one)

200.description: Contains the new SCIM bearer token in PLAINTEXT. Only its SHA-256 hash is persisted, so this is the single opportunity to copy the value; the previously issued token stops working immediately.

get.summary: Start an OAuth 2.0 / OIDC login and get the IdP redirect URL

200.description: The authorization URL to send the browser to, with client id, redirect URI, scopes and a freshly minted single-use `state` (valid 10 minutes). No client secret is included — the secret is only used server-side during the code exchange.
Success. JSON responses are wrapped in the standard envelope: `{ "data": ... }`, with optional `meta` (e.g. pagination) on list endpoints.

meta.description: Optional metadata (pagination, counts) — present on list endpoints

get.summary: Start a SAML 2.0 login and get the IdP redirect URL

200.description: The IdP SSO URL carrying the base64 `SAMLRequest` and the organization id as `RelayState`. The request ID is remembered for 10 minutes so the callback can enforce `InResponseTo`.
Success. JSON responses are wrapped in the standard envelope: `{ "data": ... }`, with optional `meta` (e.g. pagination) on list endpoints.

meta.description: Optional metadata (pagination, counts) — present on list endpoints

400.description: Validation failed — the request body does not match the documented schema (unknown properties are rejected).

post.summary: Check which login method an email must use (authenticated)

200.description: Resolved against the caller's own organization: `sso` only when SSO is enabled, enforced, the email domain is verified and the address is not on the bypass list.

400.description: Validation failed — the request body does not match the documented schema (unknown properties are rejected).

post.summary: Public pre-auth probe: does this email have to log in via SSO?

200.description: Unauthenticated probe used by the login screen, throttled to 30 requests per minute and IP. Unknown organization slugs answer `password` so the endpoint reveals nothing about which organizations or accounts exist.

400.description: Validation failed — the request body does not match the documented schema (unknown properties are rejected).

429.description: More than 30 probes from this IP within the current minute: code `RATE_LIMITED`, `params: { limit: 30, retryAfterSeconds }`. The `Retry-After` header carries the same number of seconds until the window resets.

get.summary: List the IdP attribute → Studio role mappings

200.description: Raw `pro_sso_role_mappings` rows (snake_case) ordered by descending priority, then oldest first — the same order in which they are evaluated during login. Empty array when the organization has no SSO configuration.

post.summary: Create a role mapping

201.description: The inserted `pro_sso_role_mappings` row as returned by `RETURNING *`.

400.description: Validation failed — the request body does not match the documented schema (unknown properties are rejected).

200.description: The updated `pro_sso_role_mappings` row, re-read after the write. Mappings of another organization's configuration are not addressable — they answer 404.

400.description: Validation failed — the request body does not match the documented schema (unknown properties are rejected).

200.description: Acknowledgement. An unknown id — or one belonging to another organization — answers 404 instead.

get.summary: SCIM 2.0: list or filter users

200.description: An RFC 7644 ListResponse — SCIM's own paging envelope, sent as the bare top-level body. `count` is clamped to 200. Supported filters are `userName eq "…"` and `externalId eq "…"`; anything else answers a SCIM 400 error body.

400.description: SCIM error body. `scimType` is `invalidFilter` for an unsupported filter and `invalidValue` for a body or parameter that failed validation.

401.description: SCIM error body — the bearer token is missing or unknown. Sent with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="SCIM"`.

post.summary: SCIM 2.0: provision a user

201.description: The provisioned user as a SCIM core User resource, sent as the bare top-level body. The account is created without a password, so it can only be used through SSO. A duplicate `userName` answers a SCIM 409 error body instead.

400.description: SCIM error body. `scimType` is `invalidFilter` for an unsupported filter and `invalidValue` for a body or parameter that failed validation.

401.description: SCIM error body — the bearer token is missing or unknown. Sent with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="SCIM"`.

409.description: SCIM error body with `scimType: "uniqueness"` — a user with this `userName` already exists.

get.summary: SCIM 2.0: get a single user

200.description: The user as a SCIM core User resource, sent as the bare top-level body and scoped to the organization the presented bearer token belongs to. Unknown ids answer a SCIM 404 error body.

401.description: SCIM error body — the bearer token is missing or unknown. Sent with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="SCIM"`.

404.description: SCIM error body — no user with this id in the organization the token belongs to.

patch.summary: SCIM 2.0: patch a user (activate/deactivate, name, email)

200.description: The patched user as a SCIM core User resource, sent as the bare top-level body. Only `replace`/`add` on `active`, `name.givenName`, `name.familyName`, `emails` and path-less value objects are applied; other operations are ignored.

400.description: SCIM error body. `scimType` is `invalidFilter` for an unsupported filter and `invalidValue` for a body or parameter that failed validation.

401.description: SCIM error body — the bearer token is missing or unknown. Sent with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="SCIM"`.

404.description: SCIM error body — no user with this id in the organization the token belongs to.

200.description: The updated user as a SCIM core User resource, sent as the bare top-level body. Only name, primary email and `active` are taken from the payload; omitted fields keep their current value.

400.description: SCIM error body. `scimType` is `invalidFilter` for an unsupported filter and `invalidValue` for a body or parameter that failed validation.

401.description: SCIM error body — the bearer token is missing or unknown. Sent with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="SCIM"`.

404.description: SCIM error body — no user with this id in the organization the token belongs to.

401.description: SCIM error body — the bearer token is missing or unknown. Sent with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="SCIM"`.

404.description: SCIM error body — no user with this id in the organization the token belongs to.

get.summary: SCIM 2.0 discovery: supported service-provider capabilities

200.description: Static capability document, sent as the bare top-level body: PATCH and filtering are supported, bulk / sort / ETag / password change are not, and the only authentication scheme is a bearer token.

get.summary: SCIM 2.0 discovery: supported resource types

200.description: Static ListResponse with the single supported resource type, `User`, sent as the bare top-level body.

get.summary: SCIM 2.0 discovery: supported schemas

200.description: Static ListResponse describing the core User schema and the four attributes this implementation honours (`userName`, `name`, `emails`, `active`), sent as the bare top-level body.

get.summary: List all themes of the organization (active first, then presets, then by name)

200.description: Every theme row of the caller's organization; empty array before any theme or preset was created.

post.summary: Create a custom theme

201.description: The created theme row. The response additionally carries a `contrastWarnings` array (`ProThemeContrastWarningDto`) next to `data` — non-blocking on create.

400.description: Validation failed — the request body does not match the documented schema (unknown properties are rejected).

get.summary: Get the theme currently applied to the organization

200.description: The active theme row; `data` is null when the organization runs the built-in default design.

get.summary: Get a single theme by ID

200.description: The theme row; 404 when the ID does not belong to the caller's organization.

put.summary: Update a custom theme (preset themes must be duplicated first)

400.description: Validation failed — the request body does not match the documented schema (unknown properties are rejected).

post.summary: Import a `roadbeat-theme-v1` payload as a new (inactive) theme

201.description: The imported theme row. Payloads above 64 KB or with a foreign `_format` are rejected with 400.

200.description: Light and dark CSS custom-property blocks generated from the theme (sanitized values).

get.summary: Get the organization branding configuration

200.description: The branding row; it is auto-created with defaults on the first read.

put.summary: Update the organization branding configuration (partial update)

200.description: The updated branding row, with a `warnings` array added when an asset URL points at an external host (IMP-PRO-WL-08).

400.description: Validation failed — the request body does not match the documented schema (unknown properties are rejected).

post.summary: Reset all branding fields (logos, titles, login page, footer, theme, accessibility) to defaults

201.description: The branding row after the reset — all customizable fields cleared.

put.summary: Update the organization-wide accessibility defaults (merged into the existing settings)

200.description: The full branding row, whose `accessibility` object carries the merged settings.

400.description: Validation failed — the request body does not match the documented schema (unknown properties are rejected).

get.summary: Get the full resolved branding (config + active theme + generated CSS variables) for the admin UI

200.description: Contract with the Angular `ResolvedBranding` type; `theme` and `cssVariables` are null when no theme is active.

get.summary: Get the login-safe branding subset for the pre-authentication login screen (unauthenticated)
get.description: Resolves the organization from `?org=<slug>` or the request Host header. Unknown orgs get an all-null default payload so the route cannot be used as an existence oracle. Rate limited to 60 requests/minute per IP (429) and cached for 60 s with ETag/If-None-Match.

parameters.name: org
parameters.description: Organization slug; when omitted the Host header is matched against `organizations.domain`.

200.description: Login-safe branding subset. Never includes ids, organization identifiers or `custom_css`.

304.description: Not modified — the supplied `If-None-Match` matches the cached ETag.

429.description: Rate limit exceeded (60 requests per minute per IP).

code.description: Stable machine-readable error code (e.g. BAD_REQUEST, UNAUTHORIZED, NOT_FOUND)

message.description: Human-readable message; validation errors return one message per violation

path.description: Request path that produced the error

requestId.description: Correlation ID (echoes the X-Request-Id header) for support and log lookup

errors.description: Present on 422 content-validation failures: one entry per rule that failed. Absent otherwise.

path.description: JSON pointer to the offending field

keyword.description: The rule that fired, e.g. required, after_field, before_field, requiredIf, requiredUnless, asset_exists, reference_exists

from.description: Window start. Defaults to 30 days before generation when the request omits `from`.

to.description: Window end. Defaults to the generation time when the request omits `to`.

type.description: The requested report type, echoed back.

dateRange.description: The window the report actually covers.

summary.description: Per-type roll-up. `totalEntries` is always present; the remaining keys depend on `type` — user-access adds `uniqueUsers`, `logins`, `logouts`; data-changes adds `creates`, `updates`, `deletes`, `publishes`; permission-changes adds `roleChanges`, `invites`; api-access adds `apiKeyCreated`, `apiKeyDeleted`; gdpr-data-export adds `userId` and the string array `resourcesAffected`. Documented as an open object because the key set is chosen at runtime.

entries.description: The matching audit rows, newest first, capped at 10 000 by the generator. Includes the tamper-evidence hash columns, since the report is meant to be independently verifiable.

totalEntries.description: Total rows matching the report's filters. Can exceed `entries.length` when the 10 000-row cap applies.

id.description: Identifier to pass as `type` when generating or exporting the report.

description.example: All login/logout events and session activity

available.description: Whether the report's underlying event source is actually wired on this host (IMP-PRO-AUDIT-05). Generating an unavailable type is rejected with 400 rather than returning an empty report — currently `api-access` is unavailable until CE emits api_key events.

success.description: True when the DELETE affected at least one row. False when nothing matched — a wrong ID, another organization's row, or (for saved searches) a search owned by a different user.

id.description: Audit entry ID: UUID in a `TEXT` column (migration 001 — `gen_random_uuid()::TEXT`), generated in `AuditService.log()`. Not a numeric surrogate key, so nothing here is driver-dependent and no bigint→number coercion is involved; the value is a string on the wire in every case.

organization_id.description: Owning organization; every query is scoped to the caller's org.

user_id.description: Actor who performed the action. Null for system-generated events with no user context. After a GDPR erasure scrub (migration 005) this holds the deterministic pseudonym `erased-user-<16 hex>` instead of the original user ID — an HMAC-SHA-256 of the user ID keyed by the server-side `AUDIT_PSEUDONYM_SECRET` plus the organization ID. Pseudonyms are stable for a given secret, so activity still correlates; changing (or first setting) the secret changes newly minted pseudonyms, so a subject erased on both sides of that change appears under two values.

user_email.description: Actor e-mail at the time of the event. Null when unknown; replaced by the `erased-user-<16 hex>` pseudonym after an erasure scrub.

action.description: What happened. System events use the known action vocabulary (create, update, delete, publish, unpublish, login, logout, password_change, invite, role_change, settings_change, export, import, bulk_action, api_key_create, api_key_delete, audit_verify, retention_prune, deprovision, login_blocked, erase); the column itself is free text, so filters — not the stored value — are enum-restricted.

resource.description: Entity kind the action targeted (content, content_type, user, role, asset, webhook, api_key, organization, settings, locale, plugin). Free text in the column; enum-restricted on query filters.

resource_id.description: ID of the affected entity, when the event targets one. Rewritten to the `erased-user-<16 hex>` pseudonym for rows pointing at an erased subject.

resource_label.description: Human-readable label for the affected entity (slug, title, e-mail). E-mail-like substrings belonging to an erased subject are pseudonymized in place.

changes.description: Field-level diff, or null when the event carries none. Keys are field names of the audited entity; each value is an object `{ "old": <any>, "new": <any> }`. Values are arbitrary JSON, so the shape is intentionally not modelled further. Two filters are applied to EVERY entry before it is persisted, regardless of origin (IMP-PRO-AUDIT-06 — platform-computed diffs and diffs supplied in the body of POST /pro/audit alike): fields whose name matches password / secret / token / api-key / credential / private-key become `{ "old": "[REDACTED]", "new": "[REDACTED]" }`, and any single value serializing to more than 2000 characters is replaced by the marker `[TRUNCATED <n> chars]`. Redaction runs before the tamper-evidence hash, so the chain covers the redacted row that is actually stored. A manually supplied value that is not in `{ old, new }` form is size-capped and kept as-is rather than reshaped.

metadata.description: Free-form event context, `{}` when nothing was recorded. Producer-defined; the service itself writes a `type` discriminator for internal bookkeeping rows — `chain_verification` (a verify run, plus its result fields), `retention_checkpoint` (`policyId`, `policyName`, `deleted`, `tailHash` — the hash anchoring the surviving chain across a prune) and `erasure_scrub` (`pseudonym`, `scrubbed`).

Null on the first chained row and on legacy rows written before migration 004. A non-null value on the oldest surviving row is legitimate only when a `retention_checkpoint` entry records that same hash as its `tailHash`.

entry_hash.description: Tamper-evidence chain link: unkeyed SHA-256 over `prev_hash` plus the canonicalized row fields (IMP-PRO-AUDIT-04). Null for rows written before migration 004 — those are counted as `legacyRows`, not failures, by GET /pro/audit/verify. This is a digest of data the caller can already read; no secret or signing key is involved, so it cannot be used to prove authorship — anyone able to write the table can recompute it.

valid.description: True when no broken link was found AND the chain start is properly anchored. What that does and does not establish: it detects careless or partial tampering (a row edited, re-attributed or re-ordered without rebuilding the chain), accidental mutation such as a stray UPDATE or a bad restore, and truncation — history removed without an authorized retention run leaving its `retention_checkpoint` anchor (reported via `anchored`). It does NOT detect a determined attacker with direct write access to `pro_audit_logs`: because the digests are unkeyed and cover only row data, such an attacker can rewrite history and recompute a fully self-consistent chain, after which this field still reads true. Treat `valid: true` as "no evidence of tampering", not as cryptographic proof of integrity; the defences against a privileged writer are the append-only database trigger, least-privilege DB credentials, and off-host log shipping.
